report.trigger: The third-party payment gateway had a burst of 503 errors. On checkout-api-3, payment_gateway_5xx_rate was above zero from 09:19:40Z to 09:21:35Z and peaked at 87%.
report.root_cause: Deploy dep-8841 (commit a3f9c2e, finished 09:14:47Z) changed the retry policy in checkout/payment_client.py. It added 503 to status_forcelist, set allowed_methods=None so POST charges are now retried, and set backoff_factor=0. Each failing charge was therefore tried up to 4 times with no pause between attempts. Because handle_checkout() keeps its DB connection open through the whole gateway call, retries included (this is by design), a checkout under the gateway burst held its connection for about 30 to 40 seconds instead of about 10. That filled the per-instance QueuePool (15 connections, pool_timeout=10s). Once the pool was full, every endpoint on the instance failed.
report.failure_mode: Customers got generic HTTP 503s on every endpoint, not just checkout. Most came from checkout-api itself when a request waited 10s for a DB connection and timed out (reason=db_pool_checkout_timeout, 105 requests). These hit GET /orders/{id} (42), GET /cart (26) and POST /checkout (37). Only 19 were 503s passed through from the gateway. Checkout p95 latency rose to about 40s and read-request p95 reached 10s. The checkout 5xx rate peaked at about 71%, from 09:20:00Z to 09:21:30Z.
contributing_factors: By design, the DB connection is held for the entire gateway call, retries included, so how long a connection is held depends on how the gateway behaves.
backoff_factor=0 fires the retries back-to-back, which lengthens hold time and adds load on a gateway that is already failing.
allowed_methods=None lets non-idempotent POST /checkout charges be retried, which risks double charges.
All endpoints share one pool of 15 connections per instance with pool_timeout=10s, so exhaustion caused by checkout also takes down the read endpoints.
ruled_out: Gateway outage alone: with the old retry policy, the same burst gave 93 gateway 503s on POST /checkout only. There were 0 pool timeouts, 0 read-endpoint 503s and 0 seconds of pool saturation, so the gateway alone does not explain the failures on /cart and /orders.
CPU or overall load: cpu_percent stayed around 30-36% throughout, and the traces show the time spent waiting on db.acquire_connection and on gateway calls, not on compute.
The deploy by itself, with no trigger: replaying without the gateway burst gave 0 503s and checkout p95 of 226ms.

A database-side problem: failing traces show db.acquire_connection timing out after exactly 10000ms with pool_in_use=15/15, which points to exhaustion of the app's own pool rather than a slow database. Working checkout traces acquired a connection in about 4ms.
report.counterfactual_evidence: All replays used the same 5576 requests. As deployed: 124 503s (105 pool timeouts, 19 gateway), 68 of them on read requests, 76s of pool saturation, checkout p95 40568ms. Reverting only the retry policy: 93 503s, all gateway 503s on checkout, 0 pool timeouts, 0 seconds saturated, read p95 49ms. Releasing the connection before the gateway call, with the new retries kept: 33 503s, all gateway, 0 pool timeouts, 0 read-request 503s, but checkout p95 was still 37938ms. Pool capacity 30: 33 gateway 503s, 0 pool timeouts, but 14s saturated and read p95 807ms, so a bigger pool only adds headroom. Removing the gateway burst: 0 503s. The outage needed both the burst and the new retry policy combined with the connection being held during the call.
report.documentation_evidence: No retry-library documentation was consulted. Everything said here about retry behaviour comes from the diff and from what the traces show: req-01832 made 4 POST charge attempts.
evidence_citations: The dep-8841 diff to checkout/payment_client.py: status_forcelist={502, 503, 504}, allowed_methods=None, backoff_factor=0
Trace req-01832: POST /checkout, 4 payment_gateway.charge attempts each returning 503, duration 31384ms, connection held throughout
Trace req-01884: GET /orders/{id}, db.acquire_connection timed out after 10000ms (503_pool_timeout)
Log 09:19:56.716Z checkout-api-3 ERROR: 'GET /orders/{id} failed status=503 reason=db_pool_checkout_timeout waited_ms=10000 pool_in_use=15 pool_capacity=15'
db_pool_in_use rose above 1 at 09:19:35Z, was at 15 from 09:19:50Z, and dropped back after 09:21:00Z (last point above 1 at 09:21:05Z)
Runbook: holding the connection during the payment call is by design; QueuePool pool_size=5, max_overflow=10, pool_timeout=10
report.remaining_uncertainty: The evidence covers only checkout-api-3, so the other 5 instances are assumed to behave the same but were not checked. The cause of the gateway's own burst is not known. The logs and traces did not show whether the retried POSTs created duplicate charges. The replay is a simulation and may not match production retry timing exactly.
report.recommended_fix: Right away, roll back dep-8841 (kubectl rollout undo deployment/checkout-api) or restore the old retry settings: status_forcelist={502, 504}, allowed_methods={'GET'}, backoff_factor=0.5. Do not retry POST charges unless the gateway call sends an idempotency key, and when retrying use backoff and a total time limit that is well under pool_timeout. Longer term, release the DB connection before the gateway call and reacquire it to commit, or cap how long a connection can be held during the payment call. Give read endpoints their own pool, or a separate pool reservation, so checkout traffic cannot starve them. Audit for duplicate charges from retried POSTs during 09:19:30-09:21:40Z.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Trigger: third-party gateway 503 burst (09:19:40-09:21:35). Root cause: dep-8841 retry policy (503 in status_forcelist, allowed_methods=None so POST retried, backoff 0) multiplies gateway-call time while each checkout holds a DB connection, exhausting the 15-conn pool; failure mode: 503s on all endpoints including /cart and /orders from pool timeouts.
hypotheses.supporting_evidence: req-01832: 4 POST charge attempts, 31.4s, connection held. db_pool_in_use 15/15 09:19:50-09:21:00. 503_pool_timeout traces: 42 /orders, 37 /checkout, 26 /cart vs 19 503_gateway. Diff shows retry changes.
